title: Reconnect the System
goal: By the end of this lesson, you can understand the 4 sentence types in English and practice Yes-No questions with DO/ARE to distinguish action verbs from 'to be'.
today: Practice Do you...? vs Are you...?
Answer with Yes, I do / Yes, I am

examples.text: I have a meeting with my colleague.

items.def: someone you know, but not well

examples.text: He's just an acquaintance, not a close friend.
I met an acquaintance at the conference.

items.def: you can depend on this person

examples.text: She's very reliable — always on time.
My brother is reliable. I can count on him.
He's very considerate — he always asks how I feel.
Please be considerate of other people's time.
My manager is easy-going. She never shouts.
He's easy-going — nothing stresses him out.
I get along with my coworkers.
She gets along with everyone in the family.
I lost touch with my old classmates.
We lost touch after he changed jobs.

vocab.text: Choose two people. Say who they are and one thing you like or dislike about them. Accept simple language — ask one follow-up: How do you know them? or What are they like?

head: Pattern
Example
Use
rows: I like people who listen carefully.
mệnh đề quan hệ tả người

What I like most is her honesty.

head: Want to know
Engine
Question
Answer
rows: Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
Yes, she does. / No, she doesn't.
Yes, he is. / No, he isn't.

reading.text: Honestly, I can't stand unnecessary meetings. They waste a lot of time mainly because nothing gets decided. For example, some meetings could be replaced with a short email. However, I don't mind meetings that have a clear purpose. In my experience, a short agenda makes a meeting worth the time.
Notice: can't stand + noun, don't mind + V-ing, worth + noun. These are natural ways to express opinions.

conversations.title: A new colleague
conversations.lift: find it easy to… · surprisingly well

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: How are things with your new colleague?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Good. She's very reliable — always on time.

lines.speaker: Nina
lines.text: Do you get along with her?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Yes, I do. I find it easy to talk to her.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Yes, she is. She's surprisingly well-organized too.

check: What is Tom's new colleague like?
Does Tom get along with her?
conversations.answers: 1. She's reliable and well-organized. 2. Yes, he does. 3. Yes, she is.
conversations.note: Notice: reliable, easy-going, get along with, find it easy to…

conversations.title: At the coffee machine
conversations.lift: I don't mind… · It's not that bad

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Do you like the new office coffee?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: No, I don't. I can't stand it — it's too bitter.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Really? I don't mind it. It's not that bad.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: I guess I'm just used to the old one.

lines.speaker: Anna
lines.text: Are you going to buy your own?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Yes, I am. I can't put up with this every morning.

check: Does Ben like the new coffee?
Is Ben going to buy his own?
conversations.answers: 1. No, he doesn't. 2. No, she doesn't. 3. Yes, he is.
conversations.note: Notice: can't stand, don't mind, put up with, used to

conversations.title: Weekend plans
conversations.lift: It's been ages · pick up where we left off

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I'm meeting an old friend. We lost touch years ago.

lines.speaker: Lan
lines.text: That's nice! Do you have plans to catch up?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Yes, we're going for coffee. It's been ages!

check: Did Mia lose touch with her friend?
conversations.answers: 1. Yes, she is. 2. Yes, she did. 3. Yes, they are.
conversations.note: Notice: lose touch with, catch up, It's been ages

exercises.text: Đáp án: 1 reliable · 2 easy-going · 3 considerate · 4 acquaintance. Which clue helped you choose each word? Gạch chân từ gợi ý trước khi chọn.
Đáp án: 1 Do · 2 Are · 3 Does · 4 Is · 5 Do · 6 Are. Quy tắc: action verb → DO/DOES, BE information → ARE/IS.

speaking.text: Question lab · What can't you stand?
Is there anything you can't stand at work or in daily life?

items: I can't stand waiting in traffic.

speaking.text: Use: I can't stand + noun / V-ing. Ask a partner: What about you?

roleplay.title: 60-second engine challenge
roleplay.context: Work with a partner. Take turns asking and answering Yes-No questions with DO and ARE.
steps: Partner B answers: Yes, I do. / No, I don't.
Partner A asks: Are you…? (BE information)
Partner B answers: Yes, I am. / No, I'm not.
Switch roles. Keep it fast — 10 seconds per question.
roleplay.useful: Do you work nearby? · Are you busy today? · Does she work in sales? · Is he your manager?

finalTask.text: Work with a partner. Have a 3-minute conversation about people you know. Use DO/ARE questions and answer with full sentences.
Goal: 10+ questions, 10+ full answers. Notice when you use DO vs ARE.
